concerns.text: The three Edge Cases specify MUST behaviors (log warning and halt on empty API result; filter rows with undeterminable oxidation states and log excluded count; raise ValueError when dataset <50 samples) but no FR covers any of them. FR-006 covers only descriptor gaps, not empty result sets or the minimum-sample guard. Add FRs (e.g., FR-007..FR-009) anchoring these edge-case behaviors so they are implementable and testable.

FR-001 (and other FRs) reference IDs like "US-1", "US-2", "US-3" (e.g., "(See US-1)") but no such IDs are defined elsewhere in the document. Cross‑references should resolve to an existing identifier or be removed/renamed.

The primary actor is called a "researcher" in the user stories, while the surrounding sections use the generic term "user" (e.g., "User Scenarios & Testing"). Consistent terminology for the same role should be used throughout to avoid confusion.

The paired t-test criterion is stated as 'at α=0.05 to confirm the model is not performing random guessing.' A paired t-test of predictions vs. DFT ground truth tests whether the mean difference differs from zero; a GOOD model yields p>0.05 (no significant bias), while 'random guessing' is not what this test detects. As written, an implementer cannot know which outcome constitutes success. Restate the pass condition, e.g. 'the paired t-test reports no significant mean difference (p>0.05) between predictions and DFT values on the held-out set.'

The idea's methodology explicitly specifies a held-out test set of '20% of data', but the spec defers this to '[deferred] of data' / 'held-out [deferred] test set'. The [deferred] convention covers empirical measurements, not a design split ratio the source idea already fixed. State the 20% split (or justify a change).

The idea's methodology sketch requires 'Document all code and data preprocessing steps in reproducible Jupyter notebook'. No FR or user story covers reproducible documentation of the pipeline. Add a requirement or note the deliberate deferral to the plan stage.

FR-004 states that the model will be evaluated on a held‑out test set *and* that 5‑fold cross‑validation will be run. The spec does not explicitly guarantee that the held‑out test set is disjoint from the data used in the cross‑validation folds. If the same records appear in both procedures, performance estimates become circularly biased.

FR-004 requires a paired t‑test comparing model predictions to DFT ground‑truth values. A paired t‑test assumes the paired differences are independent and normally distributed; it is not a standard metric for assessing predictive model performance and may give misleading significance results. Consider using confidence intervals on RMSE/MAE or a non‑parametric signed‑rank test instead.
